Do: Solve YOUR pain first — be Customer Zero (Giantiny ①)
Dont: Don't solve problems you READ about but never LIVE
Example_Good: Pieter Levels built NomadList from his own nomad pain
Example_Bad: Building a farming app because you read farming is big
Impact_Preview: Solving your own problem ensures authentic product quality. $0 cost, 1-2 weeks self-reflection. Founders who are Customer Zero ship 40% faster.

Do: Check if your unique skills make you 10x better at solving this
Dont: Don't build in domains where you have no unfair advantage
Example_Good: Designer building design tools (Jang/EaseUI)
Example_Bad: Accountant building social media app
Impact_Preview: Specific knowledge validation takes 1 week. Prevents 3-6 months wasted building in wrong domain. Zero cost — just honest self-assessment.

Do: Fill all 9 blocks of Lean Canvas BEFORE writing code
Dont: Don't start coding without documenting assumptions
Example_Good: Complete Lean Canvas with each block as testable hypothesis
Example_Bad: Jump straight to code 'because I know what to build'
Impact_Preview: Lean Canvas takes 2-4 hours. Saves avg 2 months of building wrong thing. Free template, forces hypothesis clarity before code.

Do: Create model big competitors can't copy (Giantiny ②)
Dont: Don't compete on features alone — that's a losing game
Example_Good: Basecamp flat pricing — enterprise players can't follow
Example_Bad: Try to out-feature Salesforce with 2 people
Impact_Preview: Counter-positioning creates structural moat. Takes 1-2 weeks to define. If successful, big competitors can't copy without self-disruption.

Do: Ask about their life not your idea — seek facts not opinions
Dont: Don't pitch your idea during validation interviews
Example_Good: 'Tell me about the last time you had this problem'
Example_Bad: 'Would you use an app that does X?' (leading question)
Impact_Preview: 10 Mom Test interviews take 2-3 weeks. Prevents building product nobody wants. $0 cost, reveals real pain vs imagined problems.

Do: Conduct at least 10 customer interviews before deciding
Dont: Don't validate with less than 10 people — sample too small
Example_Good: 10 diverse interviews revealing consistent patterns
Example_Bad: 3 friends said it's cool — must be validated
Impact_Preview: 10 interviews take 2-3 weeks. Pattern recognition starts at interview 7-8. Statistically meaningful sample prevents false validation.

Do: Use surveys for quantitative data AFTER qualitative interviews
Dont: Don't use surveys as primary validation — too shallow
Example_Good: Surveys confirm patterns found in 10+ interviews
Example_Bad: Send Google Form to 100 people — call it validated
Impact_Preview: Surveys cost $0-50, take 1-2 days. But produce shallow data — use only AFTER qualitative interviews reveal patterns to quantify.

Do: Choose tech stack one person can operate end-to-end (Giantiny ③)
Dont: Don't pick complex stack requiring dedicated DevOps
Example_Good: Vercel + Supabase + Stripe = 1 person runs everything
Example_Bad: Kubernetes + microservices for MVP with 0 users
Impact_Preview: 1-person operable stack saves $5-50K/yr in DevOps. Vercel+Supabase+Stripe = full stack for $0-29/mo. Wrong choice = 2-4 months rewrite.

Do: Set up analytics BEFORE launching MVP — not after
Dont: Don't launch without tracking — you'll fly blind
Example_Good: PostHog/Mixpanel installed before first user
Example_Bad: Built product for 3 months — no idea who uses what
Impact_Preview: PostHog free tier covers 1M events/mo. Setup takes 2-4 hours. Without it, you'll fly blind for 1-3 months before realizing.

Do: Build the ONE workflow that delivers core value
Dont: Don't add features before core loop works and retains
Example_Good: Notion: create page + organize + share (core loop)
Example_Bad: Build settings page before the main feature works
Impact_Preview: Core loop focus saves 2-4 weeks vs feature bloat. Build ONE workflow that delivers value. Everything else is post-PMF.

Rule: Use Media as lever from day 1
Do: Start creating content alongside building (Giantiny ③)
Dont: Don't wait until launch to start content — build audience now
Example_Good: Write build-in-public posts while building MVP
Example_Bad: Wait 6 months until 'product is ready' to write anything
Impact_Preview: Content created during build phase compounds. 3 months build-in-public → 500+ followers at launch. $0 cost, 2-3 hrs/week.

Do: Build simplest thing that works — optimize after PMF
Dont: Don't architect for scale before you have 100 users
Example_Good: SQLite for first 1K users → migrate to Postgres at scale
Example_Bad: Setting up sharded database before first signup
Impact_Preview: Simple architecture saves 1-3 months dev time. SQLite → Postgres migration takes 1 day when needed. Over-engineering costs 4-8 weeks.

Do: Run Sean Ellis survey — need ≥40% 'very disappointed'
Dont: Don't scale acquisition before confirming PMF
Example_Good: Monthly PMF survey tracking trend toward 40%
Example_Bad: Spending $50K on ads with 15% 'very disappointed' score
Impact_Preview: Sean Ellis survey takes 30 min to set up, 1-2 weeks to collect. Prevents premature scaling which wastes $10-50K+ on wrong channel.

Do: Integrate deeply into customer workflow (Giantiny ④)
Dont: Don't make it easy for customers to leave
Example_Good: User data + templates + team workflows all in your product
Example_Bad: CSV export makes leaving trivial
Impact_Preview: Switching costs take 1-3 months to build. Each integration makes user 20-40% less likely to churn. Data lock-in = strongest retention.

Do: Find and double down on #1 channel (Bullseye)
Dont: Don't spread across 5+ channels — you'll be mediocre at all
Example_Good: All-in on content marketing → 80% of traffic from blog
Example_Bad: Running ads + SEO + partnerships + events + influencers simultaneously
Impact_Preview: Focusing on 1 channel saves 10-20 hrs/week vs splitting effort. 80/20 rule: top channel drives 80% of growth.

Do: Optimize profit margin — financial fat = independence (Giantiny ④)
Dont: Don't grow at all costs — profitability enables survival
Example_Good: $500K revenue with 70% margin → $350K profit
Example_Bad: $2M revenue with -30% margin → burning through runway
Impact_Preview: Profit-first approach creates 6-12 month runway buffer. $500K revenue at 70% margin = $350K cash vs $2M at -30% = burning.

Do: Keep any single channel <70% of distribution
Dont: Don't depend entirely on one platform's algorithm
Example_Good: 30% SEO + 30% email + 25% community + 15% other
Example_Bad: 95% of traffic from Google — one algorithm update = dead
Impact_Preview: Diversifying distribution takes 2-3 months. Prevents existential risk: 1 algorithm change can kill 95% traffic overnight.

Do: Automate with code before hiring humans (Giantiny ③)
Dont: Don't hire when a script would do
Example_Good: Automated onboarding + billing + support → hire at $1M ARR
Example_Bad: Hired customer success team at $50K MRR
Impact_Preview: One automation script saves 5-20 hrs/week. Cost: 2-4 hrs to build. Hiring instead costs $3-6K/mo for same output.

Do: Write SOPs for every repeatable process
Dont: Don't delegate tribal knowledge — it doesn't transfer
Example_Good: Step-by-step SOPs in Notion for every process
Example_Bad: 'Just figure it out like I did' → new hire fails
Impact_Preview: SOPs take 1-2 hours per process. Saves 2-4 weeks onboarding time per new hire. Without them: 60% higher new hire failure rate.

Rule: Bootstrap is valid — evaluate freedom cost
Do: Calculate the 'freedom cost' of taking VC money (Giantiny ④)
Dont: Don't default to raising money — it's not always the answer
Example_Good: $100K profit/year bootstrapped > $0 salary with VC pressure
Example_Bad: Raised $5M → lost board control → forced to pivot
Impact_Preview: Bootstrap preserves 100% control. VC trade: $1M for 20-30% equity + board pressure + forced growth. Freedom cost is permanent.

Do: Establish at least 1 of 3 Micro-MOATs by Stage 5 (Giantiny ⑤)
Dont: Don't ignore defense — features alone are indefensible
Example_Good: Open template marketplace → users create value for each other
Example_Bad: Relied only on feature advantage → competitor copied in 3 months
Impact_Preview: Micro-MOAT takes 3-6 months to build. Without one, competitors copy features in 3 months. Network effects compound over time.

Do: Master repeating a sustainable process — boring is good
Dont: Don't chase exciting new things when process is working
Example_Good: Running same growth playbook for 12 months → compounding
Example_Bad: Pivoting strategy every 2 weeks because it's 'not working fast enough'
Impact_Preview: Consistent process for 12 months creates compound returns. Switching strategy every 2 weeks resets progress to zero each time.

Do: Complete 3-week structured trial: vision (W1) → build together (W2) → hard conversations (W3)
Dont: Don't skip trial because 'we're friends so it'll work out'
Example_Good: 2-week build sprint revealed work style incompatibility — saved both founders years of conflict
Example_Bad: Best friends started company without trial → co-founder conflict at month 6 → company dead
Impact_Preview: 21-day trial costs 3 weeks but saves years of co-founder conflict. 65% of startups fail due to co-founder issues.

Do: 4-year vesting with 1-year cliff — always — even married couples
Dont: Don't do handshake equity deals or skip vesting 'because we trust each other'
Example_Good: Co-founder left at month 8 — vesting meant they only kept 0% (cliff not met)
Example_Bad: Co-founder left at month 3 with 50% of company — no vesting agreement
Impact_Preview: Vesting setup costs $500-1500 (lawyer/Clerky). Without it: co-founder leaves with 50% of company — irreversible equity loss.

Do: Validate your idea FIRST then incorporate — not the other way around
Dont: Don't file LLC/Corp as your first startup activity
Example_Good: Validated with 15 interviews →confirmed demand → incorporated at Stage 2
Example_Bad: Filed Delaware C-Corp on day 1 → idea failed at month 2 → wasted $1500
Impact_Preview: Premature incorporation costs $500-1500. Validation first (free) prevents wasting legal fees if idea fails within 2 months.

Rule: Launch with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
Do: Ship ToS + Privacy Policy before public launch — use generators like Termly ($99)
Dont: Don't launch a product that collects user data without legal protection
Example_Good: Used TermsFeed to generate privacy policy in 30 min before launch
Example_Bad: Launched SaaS without ToS → user dispute → no legal ground to stand on
Impact_Preview: ToS + Privacy Policy via Termly/TermsFeed costs $99-200. Without them: no legal ground in user disputes. Setup takes 30-60 min.

Do: Run Van Westendorp price sensitivity survey with 30+ responses before setting price
Dont: Don't pick a price based on gut feeling or what competitors charge
Example_Good: Van Westendorp survey revealed optimal price was 2x what founder assumed
Example_Bad: Set price at $9/mo because 'that seems fair' — left 3x revenue on the table
Impact_Preview: Van Westendorp survey takes 1-2 weeks, 30+ responses. Often reveals optimal price is 2x founder's assumption — 3x revenue uplift.

Rule: Default to simple pricing — complexity kills conversion
Do: Keep pricing page to 3 tiers maximum — decision fatigue reduces conversion
Dont: Don't create 5+ pricing tiers with feature matrices nobody reads
Example_Good: Basecamp: one plan $99/mo → zero pricing confusion → high conversion
Example_Bad: Enterprise SaaS with 7 tiers + add-ons + custom → 50% of visitors leave pricing page
Impact_Preview: Simple pricing (1-3 tiers) improves conversion 15-30% vs complex pricing. Basecamp model: $99/mo flat → zero confusion.

Rule: Track ONE North Star metric per stage
Do: Each stage has exactly one metric that matters most — focus on that
Dont: Don't build 15-metric dashboards at Stage 3 — you'll drown in data
Example_Good: Stage 4: tracked only Sean Ellis score → reached 42% → knew PMF confirmed
Example_Bad: Tracked 20 metrics simultaneously → couldn't tell if product was working
Impact_Preview: North Star metric focus saves 5-10 hrs/week analyzing noise. One metric per stage prevents dashboard paralysis.

Rule: Pair every vanity metric with a real one
Do: If you report signups also report activation rate — always pair vanity with reality
Dont: Don't celebrate vanity metrics in isolation — they create false confidence
Example_Good: Reported '10K signups (2K activated)' → honest picture → focused on activation
Example_Bad: Celebrated 10K signups without mentioning only 200 were active
Impact_Preview: Pairing vanity + real metrics takes 5 min per report. Prevents false confidence: 10K signups means nothing if only 200 active.

Do: Run 8-question self-assessment (80pts max) on the 1st of every month
Dont: Don't wait until you're burned out to check — prevention > cure
Example_Good: Monthly check caught score dropping from 62 to 41 → adjusted before crisis
Example_Bad: Ignored stress for 6 months → complete burnout → 3-month recovery break
Impact_Preview: Monthly self-assessment takes 10 min. Catching burnout early (score 40→62) prevents 3-month recovery break that kills momentum.

Do: Reserve 25% of daily energy for recovery — non-negotiable (Giantiny philosophy: sustainable > fast)
Dont: Don't sacrifice sleep/exercise/relationships 'because the startup needs me'
Example_Good: Founder who sleeps 8hrs + exercises daily outperforms 80hr/week grinder at month 12
Example_Bad: 'I'll rest when I succeed' → burnout at month 8 → startup failed
Impact_Preview: 25% daily energy reserved for recovery. Founders who maintain this outperform 80hr/week grinders by month 12.

Rule: Separate business and personal finances from day 1
Do: Open business bank account before first dollar. Track every expense.
Dont: Don't use personal card for business expenses. Don't 'figure out finances later'.
Example_Good: Mercury account opened on day 1. Wave tracks all expenses same day.
Example_Bad: 'I'll sort finances when I make money' → tax mess at year end
Impact_Preview: Business bank account setup takes 30 min, $0-10/mo. Prevents tax mess: mixing finances costs 10-40 hrs at year-end to untangle.

Rule: Set aside 30% of revenue for taxes
Do: Transfer 30% of every payment to separate tax savings. Pay quarterly estimates.
Dont: Don't spend tax money. Don't get surprised by tax bill at year end.
Example_Good: Auto-transfer 30% to tax savings on every Stripe payout
Example_Bad: Spent all revenue → $15K tax bill in April → emergency scramble
Impact_Preview: 30% tax reserve auto-transfer takes 5 min to set up. Prevents $5-20K surprise tax bill. Non-compliance penalties add 25%+.

Rule: Know your runway at all times
Do: Calculate runway monthly: cash ÷ burn = months left. Alert at 6 months.
Dont: Don't guess. Don't count expected revenue as cash. Don't ignore declining runway.
Example_Good: Monthly check: $50K cash ÷ $5K burn = 10 months. Healthy.
Example_Bad: Didn't check runway → discovered 2 months left → panic decisions
Impact_Preview: Monthly runway check takes 15 min. Early warning at 6 months gives time to cut costs. At 2 months = panic decisions.

Do: Build audience while building product. Content marketing compounds.
Dont: Don't wait until launch day to think about distribution. 'Build it and they will come' is a myth.
Example_Good: 3 months of build-in-public → 500 followers → launch day traffic ready
Example_Bad: Built for 6 months in silence → launched to zero audience → crickets
Impact_Preview: Pre-launch marketing takes 2-3 hrs/week for 3 months. Builds 500+ audience for launch day. Without it: launching to zero traffic.

Do: Find ONE channel that works. Put 80% of marketing effort there.
Dont: Don't spread across 7 channels doing each poorly. Don't chase shiny new channels.
Example_Good: Content marketing → double down → 80% of traffic from blog
Example_Bad: Tried Twitter LinkedIn YouTube TikTok Reddit all at once → none worked
Impact_Preview: Doubling down on #1 channel saves 10-15 hrs/week. 80% effort on winner vs 15% on each of 7 channels. Compounds monthly.

Rule: Build self-service docs before scaling support
Do: Answer top 10 questions in a /help page. Update monthly. Reduces 80% of tickets.
Dont: Don't hire support before documenting common questions. Don't answer the same question 50 times.
Example_Good: FAQ page answers 80% of questions → 2 tickets/day instead of 20
Example_Bad: Manual email reply to every question → 4 hours/day on support → no time to build
Impact_Preview: Self-service docs take 4-8 hrs to create. Reduces support tickets 80% — saves 3-4 hrs/day. Update monthly takes 30 min.
